features.feature: CPU, Memory, Energy, Disk and Network tabs
features.note: Five tabs with per-tab columns and a graph card. The app declares `entitlements = ["system-monitor"]`, so its sandbox shares the host PID and network namespaces and reads the host /proc read-only (docs/app-isolation.md); without it the CPU tab saw only the app and bwrap. Needs the shell that honours the entitlement; verify on Midget.
Click a header to sort; arrow shown in header.

features.feature: Process filters (all, mine, other users, system, active, inactive, windowed, GPU, selected)
features.note: All ten filters are in the sidebar and View > Filter Processes. Windowed Processes (owners of an on-screen window from the shell window list, polled each reading; native clients without an owner pid are not matched), Selected Processes (the selection and everything it started, via ppid), GPU Processes and Applications in the Last 8 Hours (start time from /proc/<pid>/stat and the boot time from /proc/stat, so no start-time history is kept) are built on the branch. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Check Windowed Processes and Applications in the Last 8 Hours on the lab machine.

features.apple: toolbar filter search field, Edit > Find
features.note: Toolbar search plus Process > Find Process (cmd+F) at main.rs:81.

SIGTERM / SIGKILL via toolbar and Process menu; no confirmation sheet. With the system-monitor entitlement the app signals through the host PID namespace, so Quit works on processes owned by the app account (kill(2) permission is unchanged: capabilities stay dropped and the user namespace stays unshared); other users and root processes still need the privileged helper, which this entitlement does not grant.
features.wire: Check the sheet on the lab machine: Return and Escape, and Force Quit as the default from its menu item.

features.note: Process > Send Signal... opens a sheet listing the eight signals with what each does, Cancel and Send. The arrow keys move the choice, Return sends and Escape closes. The submenu sends directly. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Check the sheet on the lab machine with the keyboard and with the pointer.

features.feature: Inspect Process window (stats, memory, open files and ports)
features.apple: ProcessInspector.nib: Memory, Statistics, Open Files and Ports tabs
features.note: The inspector is a panel in the window with Memory, Statistics and Open Files and Ports segments (inspect.rs detail_rows and file_and_port_lines; draw.rs draw_inspector). Ports lists the TCP and UDP sockets with endpoints and state, read from the process's own socket tables. Reveal in Files (window.rs reveal_in_files; main.rs holds the read grant) shows the program in Files. Done and Escape close it. Not a separate window: the SDK opens one window per app. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: A separate inspector window needs the SDK to open a second window; the panel stays until then.

features.note: Process > Sample Process runs a background job (sample_proc.rs run) that reads each thread's wait point and kernel stack every 20 ms for 3, 10 or 30 seconds, then shows the report in the window. Parsing and the report are unit tested in sample_proc.rs. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Check the report on the lab machine against a busy process, and that a second sample waits for the first to finish.

features.apple: View > Run Spindump, Run System Diagnostics
features.note: View > Run System Diagnostics also writes system-sample.txt: five looks, 200 ms apart, at every thread of every process (sample_proc.rs sample_system), each thread named with its process. The archive is still saved through the save panel. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Add an option to write the archive to the Desktop without the panel once the shell grants that.

features.note: Process > Show Deltas for Process stores the selected process's counters as a baseline (window.rs toggle_deltas). CPU time, bytes and GPU time then show the change (model.rs cell_text), sort by it, and the Since Baseline column shows its age. Host unit tests cover the cell text and the sort. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Check on the lab machine that the counters count from the toggle and go back to totals when it is turned off.

features.bifrost: springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/model.rs (Tab::all_columns, SortKey::RealMem, Purgeable, Kind); springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/sample.rs (parse_rollup, parse_elf_kind, Sampler scan_real, scan_purgeable, scan_kind); springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/window.rs (sync_scans)
features.note: View > Columns toggles the per-tab columns (User, Threads, PID, CPU Time, Parent PID, Ports, Private Memory, Idle Wake Ups and more), persisted. Built 2026-10-19: Real Mem (the proportional set size from smaps_rollup, so shared pages are split between the processes that map them), Purgeable (the LazyFree pages the kernel may take back, the Linux counterpart of purgeable memory) and Kind (the machine in the program's ELF header, x86_64 or ARM64) on the Memory tab, and Kind on the CPU tab. All three are off by default and read only while shown (Sampler scan flags), from one smaps_rollup read per process; a process of another user shows a dash. Tested on the host in sample.rs (the_rollup_gives_real_private_and_purgeable_memory, an_elf_header_names_the_machine), model.rs (real_memory_purgeable_and_kind_read_from_the_sample) and window.rs (real_memory_purgeable_and_kind_are_read_only_while_shown). Still missing: Compressed Mem, Real Private Mem and Real Shared Mem columns. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Midget check: open Activity Monitor, Memory tab, View > Columns, tick Real Mem, Purgeable and Kind: Real Mem is at most Memory for the same process, Kind reads x86_64 for the user's own processes and a dash for root's; untick them again and the columns go. Also check the dash for unreadable Private Memory and the wake-up rate.

features.note: View > Update Frequency has 1, 2 and 5 second radio items (main.rs), feeds the next reading (window.rs set_frequency and next_wake) and is stored in app defaults. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Check the radio items and the restored choice after a relaunch on the lab machine.

features.apple: CPU tab footer graph, Window > CPU History
features.note: View > CPU History swaps the CPU graph for one strip per core, kept in app defaults. Window > CPU History opens a floating window with the same per-core strips. Window > GPU History (built 2026-10-19) opens a floating window with the last minute of the GPU's busy share and the process using it most, and closes again from the same item; the sampler reads the GPU while the window is open (Monitor::set_gpu_window, sync_scans). The CPU load graph stays in the main window. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Midget check: open Activity Monitor, Window > GPU History: a 420 pt window titled GPU History shows Busy and bars while something draws (open the Settings window and scroll), the tick mark in the Window menu follows the window, closing it with its traffic light or cmd+w clears the tick and stops the GPU read (the GPU tab's graph is empty again on the CPU tab). With a driver that publishes no DRM counters and no vendor tool the window reads Reading the GPU.

features.feature: Floating CPU Usage window and Keep on Top
features.apple: Window > CPU Usage, Keep CPU Windows on Top
features.note: Window > CPU Usage opens a small floating window with the total and one bar per core, and closes again from the same item. Window > Keep CPU and GPU Windows on Top (renamed 2026-10-19 when the GPU History window joined) floats the open CPU and GPU windows above the normal windows and is remembered. The app opens the window with Ctx::open_window and sets its level with windows::set_window_level; the shell keeps the level per window (ToShell::WindowLevelOf, tag 0x1cc; app_window_table.rs set_floating; desk.rs floating_apps and sync_levels). Built and reviewed by reading only. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Check on Midget that the CPU Usage window stays above the other windows with Keep CPU Windows on Top on, drops back when it is off, and that its close control closes only that window.

features.note: View > Dock Icon (Application Icon, CPU, Memory, Disk, Network) puts the live figure on the Dock badge (at most four characters) with a progress bar under it, through the dock service; remembered in app defaults. The tile does not draw the scrolling graph the reference shows, because the dock service takes only a text badge, a progress bar, a bounce and menu items. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Needs an image content for the dock tile in the shell's dock service; the SDK dock_tile module sends only badge, progress, bounce and menu.

features.apple: Memory tab footer: pressure graph, app/wired/compressed, cached, swap
features.note: The Memory footer draws the PSI pressure share as a minute of bars (draw.rs draw_pressure) and a detail line of App, Kernel, Shared, Cached Files, Compressed and Swap Used (draw.rs detail line; sample.rs Memory::app, wired, file_cache, tested in meminfo_breakdown_splits_programs_kernel_shared_and_cache). The categories are Linux counters, so App and Kernel are estimates; no full pressure graph.
features.wire: Match the reference memory categories where Linux gives the same figure.

features.apple: Energy tab: Energy Impact, average, App Nap, Preventing Sleep
features.note: The 12 hr Average means persist in energy-averages.txt in the app's storage: written every minute and read at launch (model.rs EnergyAverages to_text and from_text). Energy impact is still a CPU and disk estimate. No App Nap column: a Linux analogue (cgroup freezing) needs privileges an ordinary app does not have, so it is not built. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Decide an App Nap analogue from cgroup state that an ordinary user can read.

features.feature: Disk tab: bytes per process and graph
features.note: Per-process read/write bytes from /proc/<pid>/io; system rates from diskstats.

features.apple: Network tab: sent/received bytes and packets per process
features.bifrost: springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/sample_net.rs (parse_ss, per_process, rate, read_sockets); springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/sample.rs (Sampler scan_net, net_prev); springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/model.rs (Tab::Network columns, SortKey::NetRx, NetTx, NetRxTotal, NetTxTotal, Connections); springboard/apps/activity-desktop/src/window.rs (rebuild, sync_scans, footer_text)
features.note: Built 2026-10-19: the Network tab lists processes, busiest first, with Received/s, Sent/s, Bytes Received, Bytes Sent and an optional Connections column, from the kernel's per-socket counters (ss -tinpH read once per update while the tab is shown; sample_net.rs sums them per owning process and the sampler turns the difference of two readings into a rate). The interface totals moved to the footer and the graph card still plots the interfaces. Show Deltas counts the byte totals from the baseline. Limits: TCP only (no UDP), only sockets of the user's own processes (another user's sockets carry no owner without privileges); the sandbox shares the host network namespace through the system-monitor entitlement, so ss sees the machine's sockets rather than an empty namespace, a closed socket takes its bytes with it so the totals count the sockets open now, and no packet counts yet (ss reports segs_in and segs_out). Tested on the host: sample_net.rs (parse and sum, rate), model.rs (the_network_tab_is_per_process_and_sorts_by_what_it_receives) and window.rs (the_sockets_are_read_only_on_the_network_tab_and_it_lists_the_processes_that_own_some). Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Midget check: open Activity Monitor, Network tab, and run `curl -o /dev/null https://example.com/large-file` in the Terminal: curl appears with Received/s above zero while it runs and its row is gone once it ends (its socket closes); the footer shows the interface totals; View > Columns > Connections shows the socket count. Needs `ss` (iproute2) on Midget: without it the tab reads No processes with TCP connections. Packet counts from segs_in and segs_out and UDP sockets are the remaining gap.

features.note: A GPU tab (% GPU, GPU Time, graph of the machine total) reads the DRM client counters in /proc/<pid>/fdinfo, only while the tab or the GPU filter is shown. Where the driver publishes no DRM counters (a proprietary driver), the per-process share falls back to the engine column of the vendor GPU tool's process table (sample.rs parse_pmon), read only while the GPU is shown and not asked again when the tool is absent. Window > GPU History (2026-10-19) opens the history in its own floating window through Ctx::open_window, as the CPU windows do (main.rs toggle_gpu_window, draw.rs draw_gpu_history_window); the GPU is read while it is open. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Midget check: see the CPU Load / History graphs row for the window; on the GPU tab, % GPU and GPU Time still follow the driver's counters.

features.note: Edit > Copy (cmd+C) copies the selected row as tab-separated text of the columns the tab shows (window.rs copy_text), counting from the baseline when Show Deltas is on and including the Since Baseline column when shown. Not yet verified on Midget.
features.wire: Verify on Midget that Copy writes the selected process row with visible columns, tabs intact, and baseline values when delta mode is on.
